A.explanation: Total momentum cannot fall from $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ to $2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ for an isolated system, where momentum is conserved.

B.explanation: Momentum is conserved at $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, but kinetic energy cannot increase from $30 \text{ J}$ to $90 \text{ J}$ in an inelastic sticking collision.

C.explanation: Momentum stays at $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and kinetic energy falls from $90 \text{ J}$ to $30 \text{ J}$, as required for an inelastic collision in an isolated system.

D.explanation: Momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy staying at $90 \text{ J}$ would be elastic, not inelastic with the objects moving off together.

hints: Notice the question states the two objects form an isolated system, so check which rows keep total momentum before collision equal to total momentum after collision in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Recall what inelastic means for kinetic energy when objects stick and move off together - some $\text{J}$ of kinetic energy is transferred to internal energy, so total kinetic energy must decrease.
Compare the $90 \text{ J}$ and $30 \text{ J}$ values before and after: decide which order gives a loss of kinetic energy while momentum stays at $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given conditions: one object moving, one stationary, they stick together, and the system is isolated with no external resultant force.
Apply conservation of linear momentum for an isolated system: $p_{before} = p_{after}$. So the only possible rows have $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ before and $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ after.
Apply the rule for an inelastic collision: total kinetic energy is not conserved but decreases because work is done deforming the objects and increasing internal energy.

Therefore total kinetic energy after must be less than before. A fall from $90 \text{ J}$ to $30 \text{ J}$ satisfies this, while $30 \text{ J}$ to $90 \text{ J}$ is a gain and $90 \text{ J}$ to $90 \text{ J}$ is elastic.
Momentum conserved plus kinetic energy lost matches the row with $6$ to $6 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and $90$ to $30 \text{ J}$. This is option C.
